title: Warm Quenched Tunisian Water Tagine
description: A light, earthy, and festive Tunisian dish featuring warm water and a lacquer-glaze, making it macrobiotic-friendly.
instructions: In a large clay pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional 1 minute.
Add the chopped carrot and zucchini, and cook until they start to soften, about 5 minutes.
Add the cumin, coriander, and turmeric, and stir to combine.
Add the chickpeas, chopped onion, garlic, carrot, and zucchini, and stir to combine.
Pour in the warm water, and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and let the tagine simmer, covered, for about 20 minutes.
While the tagine is cooking, prepare the lacquer-glaze by mixing the pomegranate molasses with a tablespoon of water.
Once the tagine is ready, brush the lacquer-glaze over the top.
Serve the Warm Quenched Tunisian Water Tagine hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley, if desired.
Let the dish rest for 5 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld.
